command-and-control infrastructure concept
Command-and-control infrastructure is the servers and systems attackers use to send instructions to malware and receive stolen data.
Command-and-control server concept
Remote computers controlled by attackers that send orders to infected devices and collect stolen data.
command-and-control servers concept
Remote computers controlled by attackers that send orders to infected devices and collect stolen data.
Company Servers concept
Computers operated by an organization to store data or provide services to users and other systems.
compauth concept
compauth is shown in the article as a composite authentication result for email checks.
also: compauth=pass
compliance professionals concept
Compliance professionals are people who help organizations follow laws, regulations, and internal rules.
Composite authentication concept
Composite authentication is using several identity or message-checking signals together to decide whether something is trustworthy.
compromise concept

compromised concept

compromised account concept
An account whose credentials have been stolen or guessed, allowing an attacker to impersonate the legitimate user.
compromised credentials concept
Compromised credentials are login details that have been stolen, exposed, or otherwise made unsafe.

Computers or servers that attackers have successfully taken control of.

Compromised insiders are trusted people whose accounts, devices, or actions have been taken over or influenced by attackers.

Compromised routers are network devices that attackers have taken over and can use to spy on traffic, redirect users, or hide attacks.

A compromised third party is an outside vendor or partner whose systems or accounts have been breached.
compromised websites concept
Compromised websites are legitimate websites that attackers have broken into and changed or abused for malicious purposes.

Compute means the processing power used to run software, services, or AI models.
computer intrusions technique
Unauthorized entry into a computer, account, or network.
computer systems concept
Computer systems are connected hardware and software used to process information and provide digital services.
Configuration baselines concept
Approved standard settings for systems that help keep them secure and consistent.
configuration changes concept
Configuration changes are modifications to settings that affect how a system, application, or device behaves.

A configuration file is a file that stores settings telling software how to run.
configuration files concept
Configuration files are files that store settings telling software or systems how to behave.

A verified incident in which an unauthorized party accessed, stole, exposed, or altered protected information or systems.

Confluence is Atlassian’s collaboration and documentation platform for teams.

Connecting concept
Connecting is a status meaning a device, app, or service is trying to establish a network connection.
Consent concept
A person's informed agreement to let an organization collect, use, or share their information.
conspiracy to commit wire fraud concept

Information used to contact a person, such as an address, email address, or phone number.
container concept

container images concept

containers concept
Containers are lightweight packages that run applications with their needed files in isolated environments.
continuous concept

Continuous evidence is security or compliance proof collected regularly or automatically over time.

Continuous validation means repeatedly checking that security controls, identities, or systems still work as expected instead of testing them only once.

Conventional Deployments concept

cookies concept

coordination concept
Coordination is the organized sharing of tasks, information, and decisions among people or teams.

correlation concept
Correlation means finding connections between separate events, data points, or alerts that may be related.

Rules and controls intended to stop money or other resources from being used to support terrorism.

court documents other

COVID-19 research is scientific work focused on understanding, preventing, or treating the disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus.
crates.io product

credentials concept
Credentials are login details or access tokens that prove a user or system is allowed to access something.

Credit lines are amounts of credit that a bank or lender has made available for someone to borrow.

A group of people working together to commit crimes.
critical assets concept

critical infrastructure concept
Critical infrastructure refers to essential systems and services that societies and organizations depend on.

Labels used to indicate that a security flaw could cause serious or very serious harm if exploited.

cryptocurrency wallet product

cryptocurrency wallets product
Cryptocurrency wallets are tools used to store and manage access to digital currency funds.

CSO concept
CSO usually means chief security officer, an executive responsible for an organization's security.
curl

custom rules concept
Custom rules are user-defined checks or instructions that a tool follows instead of only using its built-in behavior.
customer data concept

customer identity concept
Customer identity is the information and login details that identify a customer in an application or service.

CVSS 10.0 is the highest severity score on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System scale for rating security flaws.

CVSS 9.3 is a very high vulnerability severity score on a 0-to-10 scale used to show how serious a security flaw is.

CVSS v4.0 is version 4.0 of the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, a standard way to rate how serious a vulnerability is.
cyber concept

cyber incident concept
A cyber incident is any event where digital systems, accounts, or data may have been attacked, exposed, or disrupted.
cyber operations concept
Activities conducted in cyberspace including espionage, sabotage, or defense, typically by state-sponsored groups.
cyber resilience concept
Cyber resilience is an organization's ability to keep operating and recover quickly when cyberattacks or failures happen.
cyber risk concept
Cyber risk is the chance that digital systems, data, or operations could be harmed by security problems.
cyber verification program concept
A cyber verification program is a process for checking that security claims, controls, or requirements are actually in place.
Cyber Vulnerability vulnerability
A cyber vulnerability is a weakness in software, hardware, people, or processes that attackers could exploit.
cyberattack concept
A cyberattack is an attempt to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems or data.
cyberattacks concept
Malicious activities conducted over computer networks to steal data, disrupt operations, or damage systems.
cybercrime concept
Cybercrime is crime carried out using computers, networks, or the internet.
cybercriminals threat-actor
Cybercriminals are people who use computers or the internet to commit crimes such as fraud, theft, or extortion.

Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks, software, and data from digital attacks or misuse.
Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) organization
A U.S. government agency that helps protect civilian government systems and critical infrastructure from cyber threats.
cybersecurity firms concept
Companies that provide services and products to protect organizations from digital threats.
Cybersecurity professionals concept
Cybersecurity professionals are people whose job is to protect systems, networks, and data from digital threats.
cybersecurity requirements concept
Rules or conditions requiring people or organizations to use specified measures to protect systems and information.
cybersecurity researchers organization
Cybersecurity researchers are people who study digital threats, software flaws, and attacks to help protect systems.
cybersecurity standards concept
Cybersecurity standards are agreed rules or guidelines that organizations use to protect computers, networks, and data.
cybersecurity-and-infrastructure-security-agency organization
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency is the U.S. government agency that helps defend critical infrastructure and improve cybersecurity.

CyCognito is a cybersecurity company known for external attack surface management technology.
Cyera organization
Cyera is a cybersecurity company focused on discovering and protecting sensitive data across cloud and enterprise systems.
CyScenarioBench tool
A cybersecurity benchmark used to measure how well an AI system handles security-related tasks and restrictions.
D1 product
Cloudflare D1 is a managed SQL database service for Cloudflare applications.
d1.pool4883.pw other
d1.pool4883.pw is a domain name referenced as command-and-control infrastructure.
DarkSword malware
DarkSword is a named malware family, threat, or cyber tool referenced in security reporting.
Data access concept
Data access means the ability to view, use, change, or retrieve information from a system.
data center concept
A data center is a facility that houses servers and networking equipment for running digital services.
Data collection concept
Data collection is the process of gathering information from people, systems, devices, or services for analysis or use.
data exposure concept
Data exposure means sensitive information is left accessible to people or systems that should not be able to see it.

Data recovery firms are companies that help customers retrieve lost, damaged, deleted, or encrypted data.
also: recovery companies, recovery firms
data theft concept
Data theft is the stealing of information from a system or service.

Data was stolen means information was copied or taken by someone who was not authorized to have it.
database passwords concept
Database passwords are credentials used to access and manage data stored in a database.
Dates of birth concept
Dates of birth are personal information that can help identify someone and may be sensitive if exposed.

Decrypted sample files are example files that have been restored from encryption to demonstrate that recovery is possible.
decryption concept

defenders concept

A program tier intended to give approved users access for legitimate defensive cybersecurity work.
deleted concept
Deleted means removed from normal access, though copies may sometimes still exist in backups, logs, or recovery areas.
denial-of-service

Department of Child Safety organization
A Department of Child Safety is a government agency responsible for protecting children and responding to child-welfare concerns.
Department of Health and Human Services organization
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services is the federal agency responsible for public health and human-services programs.
Department of Justice organization
The main U.S. federal law enforcement agency responsible for prosecuting federal crimes and upholding justice.
dependency concept

Deployed in Place concept
Deployed in place describes personnel who remain at their home location while performing duties similar to a long-term deployment.
Detect technique
Detect means to identify suspicious or malicious activity in systems, networks, or data.
detection concept
Detection is the process of finding signs of suspicious or malicious activity.
detections concept
Alerts or findings generated by security tools indicating that a potential threat or malicious activity has been identified.
deterministic concept
A system or function that always produces the same output for the same input, with no random variation.
developer workflows concept
Developer workflows are the regular steps software developers use to write, test, review, and release code.

Device management is the work of setting up, maintaining, securing, and retiring an organization's computers and mobile devices.
digitalcanion other
A named source, author, or identifier referenced in security reporting.
directory listing concept

Directory traversal is a vulnerability where attackers manipulate file paths to access files they should not be able to reach.

Directory traversal requests use specially crafted file paths to try to access files outside the folder a web application should allow.
Disaster recovery concept
Disaster recovery is the process of restoring technology systems and data after a major failure, attack, or disaster.
Disaster recovery site concept
A secondary location or environment used to restore important systems after a major outage or disaster.
Disclosure concept
Disclosure is the act of reporting or publishing information about a security issue so it can be understood and fixed.
discord product
Discord is a communication platform for text, voice, and video chats, popular with gaming and online communities.
Discovery technique
Discovery is the attacker activity of learning about a victim’s systems, accounts, and network before taking further action.

A display name is the human-readable name shown for an account, sender, or object, which may differ from its real identifier.
disruption concept
Disruption is an interruption that prevents systems, services, or operations from working normally.

also: dmarc=pass

Property files are configuration files that store application settings, often as name-and-value pairs.
Proprietary Decryption Technology concept
Proprietary decryption technology is a company's own claimed method or software for restoring encrypted data.
also: tools and decryption techniques, recovery methods, special recovery methods
ProPublica organization
ProPublica is a nonprofit investigative journalism organization.
protected files concept
Protected files are files guarded by permissions or security controls so unauthorized users or programs cannot read or change them.
Protected Health Information concept
Protected Health Information is personal medical or health-related data that is legally protected from improper use or disclosure.
Protective Orders concept
Protective orders are court orders intended to restrict contact or behavior to protect a person from harm or harassment.
Proven Data organization
Proven Data is a company that provides cybersecurity incident response and data recovery services.
proxy concept
A proxy is an intermediate server that forwards internet traffic between a user and a destination.
Psychedelic Stealer malware
An information-stealing malware family that collects browser, cryptocurrency wallet, and device data.
Public disclosure concept
Public disclosure is the act of making information, such as a security flaw, available to the public.
Public internet concept
The public internet is the globally accessible network that anyone can connect to through internet service providers.
public roads concept
Public roads are streets and highways open for use by the general public.
public services concept
Services provided by government to citizens, such as healthcare or transportation.
pull request concept
A pull request is a request to review and merge code changes into a shared software project.
push technique
A push is the act of sending local code changes to a remote source-code repository such as GitHub.
Python tool
Python is a popular programming language often used to write scripts, automation tools, and security research code.
Python pickle product
Python pickle is a Python feature for saving and loading objects, but opening untrusted pickle files can be unsafe because they can execute code.
quarantined concept
Quarantined means a suspicious file, email, or system has been isolated so it cannot easily cause harm while it is investigated.
queues concept
Queues are ordered waiting lines for tasks or messages that computer systems process one at a time or in sequence.
R2 product
Cloudflare R2 is an object-storage service for storing files and other large data.
Raabby WaIIet product
A deceptive name used by a fake cryptocurrency wallet application or extension.
Rabby product
Rabby is a cryptocurrency wallet browser extension used to manage crypto assets and transactions.
Rabby Wallet product
Rabby Wallet is a cryptocurrency wallet browser extension used to interact with Ethereum and other Web3 networks.
ransom concept
A sum of money demanded by criminals to restore access to data or systems after a ransomware attack.
ransom demands concept
Ransom demands are requests from criminals for payment, usually in exchange for restoring access to stolen or encrypted data.
ransom notes concept
Ransom notes are messages from attackers demanding payment, usually after data has been encrypted or stolen.
ransom payments concept
Ransom payments are money paid to criminals in hopes of recovering data, stopping leaks, or restoring access after an attack.
also: pay the ransom
ransomware concept
Ransomware is malicious software or an operation that locks or steals data to pressure victims into paying money.
ransomware activity concept
Ransomware activity is behavior related to malware that locks or steals data and demands payment from victims.
ransomware affiliates threat-actor
Ransomware affiliates are criminals who carry out attacks using ransomware provided by another group and share the profits.
ransomware attack concept
A ransomware attack is when criminals lock files or systems and demand payment to restore access or prevent data leaks.
ransomware attacks technique
Ransomware attacks are incidents where attackers use software or methods to disrupt access and demand payment.
Ransomware deployment technique
Ransomware deployment is the stage where attackers install or run ransomware on victim systems.
Ransomware gang threat-actor
A ransomware gang is a criminal group that uses malware or data theft to demand payment from victims.
ransomware gangs threat-actor
Criminal groups that use malicious software to encrypt victims' data and demand payment for its release.
ransomware group threat-actor
A ransomware group is a criminal or threat-actor team that uses malware to lock or steal data and demand payment.
ransomware groups threat-actor
Ransomware groups are criminal teams that use ransomware or data theft to extort victims for money.
ransomware operations threat-actor
Ransomware operations are organized criminal activities that break into systems, encrypt or steal data, and demand payment.
ransomware operators threat-actor
Ransomware operators are criminals who run attacks that lock or steal data and demand payment from victims.
also: ransomers
Ransomware Remediation concept
Ransomware remediation is the work of containing a ransomware attack and restoring affected systems and data.
also: recovery and remediation services
rate-limiting concept
Rate-limiting restricts how many requests someone can make in a set time to prevent abuse or overload.
also: rate limiting rule
Read-Only concept
A permission setting that allows someone to view information but not change it.
Readiness concept
Readiness is the state of being prepared to perform a task, job, or mission effectively.
Real time concept
Real time means something happens or is shown immediately, or with very little delay.
Real-World Operations concept
Real-world operations are actions carried out against actual systems, people, or events rather than simulations or exercises.
Reasoning concept
Reasoning is the process of working through information logically to reach an answer or decision.
recommendation concept
A recommendation is suggested guidance or an action that someone should consider taking to reduce risk or solve a problem.
reconnaissance technique
Reconnaissance is the information-gathering step attackers use to learn about a target before trying to break in.
Reconnaissance workflows technique
Repeatable steps for gathering information about a target or security issue before taking further action.
also: recon workflows
Recover concept
Recover is a cybersecurity function focused on restoring systems, data, and services after an incident.
recovery phrase concept
A recovery phrase is a list of words used to restore access to a cryptocurrency wallet if the device or app is lost.
recovery phrases concept
Recovery phrases are lists of words used to restore access to a cryptocurrency wallet or other secured account.
Recovery Proofs concept
Recovery proofs are restored files or other evidence used to show that encrypted data can be recovered.
Red team concept
The offensive security team that simulates real-world attacks to test an organization's defenses and improve security.
Red Team Access product
A program tier that authorizes participants to test systems by safely simulating attacks.
Red Team Operation technique
A red team operation is an authorized security exercise in which testers act like attackers to find weaknesses.
redirect concept
A redirect sends a browser or request from one web address to another.
Redirect Parameter concept
A redirect parameter is part of a web link that tells a site where to send the visitor next.
also: redirect parameters
Registry concept
The Registry is a Windows database that stores system and application settings.
Rejetto HTTP File Server product
A software product for sharing and serving files over HTTP, also known as HFS.
remediation technique
Remediation is the work of fixing a security problem and reducing the damage it caused.
remote access concept
The ability to connect to another computer or network from a distant location and use it as if you were physically present.
Remote access controls concept
Security rules and safeguards that limit who can connect to systems from elsewhere.
remote access tool tool
A remote access tool is software that lets someone control or manage a computer from another location, which can be legitimate or abused by attackers.
Remote access tools tool
Remote access tools let someone control or manage a computer from another location, which can be legitimate or abused by attackers.
remote attacker concept
A remote attacker is someone who tries to exploit a system over a network without needing physical access to it.
remote attackers concept
Remote attackers are people who try to affect a system over a network rather than by physically accessing it.
remote browser product
A remote browser is a web browser running on another computer or in the cloud instead of directly on the user's device.
remote control technique
Remote control means operating a computer, phone, or system from another location over a network.
Remote shell tool
A remote shell is command-line access to a computer over a network.
Remote workers concept
People who do their jobs away from the employer's usual office, often from home.
remote-code-execution technique
Remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands on a system from elsewhere.
Remotely tool
Remotely is a remote administration tool that can be used to access and manage computers over a network.
Replay technique
A replay attack is when someone reuses captured data or requests to make a system repeat an action or reveal information.
repository concept
A repository is a storage location for code, files, and their change history, especially in systems like GitHub.
Reputation concept
A trust score or history used by security systems to judge whether a sender, website, or file is likely safe.
request logs concept
Records kept by a server that show incoming web or network requests.
Research University organization
A research university is a university that conducts significant academic and scientific research in addition to teaching students.
researchers organization
Researchers are people who study systems, threats, or vulnerabilities to understand and improve security.
resilience concept
The ability of an organization to anticipate, withstand, and recover from adverse cyber events and security breaches.
Respond technique
Respond means to take action after detecting a security issue, such as containing an attack or fixing affected systems.
Restart concept
A restart is turning a device or program off and then back on again to refresh it or apply changes.
Restore technique
Restore means to bring data, settings, or a system back to an earlier working state.
Restore testing concept
The practice of checking that backups can actually restore needed data and systems.
Restored clinical systems concept
Healthcare systems that have been brought back into operation after an outage or incident.
Retention concept
Retention is an organization’s ability to keep its employees or members from leaving.
Retrospective tracking concept
The practice of looking back through stored location records to reconstruct where someone traveled.
revocation concept
The process of invalidating a digital credential or certificate so it can no longer be used.
risk assessment concept
Risk assessment is the process of judging how likely and serious a security problem may be.
risk assessments concept
Risk assessments are reviews that identify what could go wrong and how serious the impact might be.
Role-Based Access Controls technique
Role-based access controls give people permissions based on their job role rather than granting everyone the same access.
root-level concept
Root-level means having the highest level of control over a device or operating system.
root-level control concept
Root-level control means having the highest level of access on a Unix-like computer, allowing almost any change to the system.
rootrun tool
rootrun is a tool or script name referenced in security reporting.
Routable address concept
A network address that other machines can reach over a network.
Router administration interfaces product
Web pages or services used to configure and manage network routers.
Royal Mail organization
Royal Mail is the United Kingdom's postal and delivery service.
Royalties concept
Royalties are payments made to creators or rights holders when their work is used or sold.
rubygems
RubyGems is the package manager and public package repository for the Ruby programming language.
run code concept
To run code means to make a computer execute instructions written in a programming language.
runtime concept
Runtime is the period when a program is actively running, or the software environment it needs in order to run.
runtime enforcement technique
A security technique that monitors and enforces policies during the execution of a program, blocking violations in real-time.
russia
Russia is a country frequently referenced in cybersecurity stories involving cybercrime groups, espionage, and government activity.
Russia-linked threat-actor
A description for threat actors or activity reported as having connections to Russia.
Russia-linked cyberattacks concept
Russia-linked cyberattacks are cyber operations attributed to or associated with Russian state, criminal, or patriotic actors.
Russian-Speaking Operation threat-actor
A Russian-speaking operation is a threat activity group described as operating primarily in Russian.
SaaS applications concept
SaaS applications are software services delivered over the internet rather than installed and managed locally by each organization.
SaaS platforms product
SaaS platforms are online software services that users access through the internet rather than installing locally.
sabotage technique
Sabotage is deliberate damage or disruption meant to weaken an organization, system, or country.
safeguards concept
Safeguards are protections put in place to reduce the chance or impact of harm, misuse, or security incidents.
SAFER product
SAFER is a U.S. motor-carrier information system run by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration.
Safety Systems concept
Automated rules, checks, and controls intended to reduce harmful or inappropriate use of a service.
sailpoint
SailPoint is an identity security company that helps organizations manage who has access to systems and data.
sandbox-escape technique
A technique where malware breaks out of a restricted, isolated testing environment to attack the real underlying system.
Sapphire Sleet threat-actor
Sapphire Sleet is a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group identified by Microsoft.
Scam messages concept
Scam messages are texts, emails, or chats designed to trick people into sending money, data, or access.
scams concept
Scams are dishonest schemes designed to trick people into giving money, information, or access.
scan the internet technique
To scan the internet means to automatically check many public systems online to find open services, devices, or weaknesses.
Scanners tool
Scanners are tools that check systems, networks, or websites for exposed services, weaknesses, or signs of compromise.
scanning technique
Scanning is checking computers, networks, or services to find what is reachable and what may be vulnerable.
scans concept
Scans are automated checks that examine software or related data for issues or information.
SCL concept
SCL is a spam confidence level score used to help decide how suspicious an email is.
also: SCL:1
scope concept
scope defines what access, targets, or permissions are included in a security test, login request, or authorization grant.
Scope Creep concept
Scope creep happens when a task gradually expands beyond its original agreed-upon limits.
scope enforcement concept
Controls that ensure a security test or automated agent only operates on systems it is authorized to access.
screenshot concept
A screenshot is a captured image of what is shown on a screen.
screenshots concept
Images that capture what is currently shown on a computer screen.
search engine results concept
Search engine results are the links and summaries shown after someone searches the web using a service like Google or Bing.
search-ms: protocol
search-ms: is a Windows URI handler that opens Windows Search results and can be abused in phishing or file-opening tricks.
SearchLeak technique
SearchLeak is a named vulnerability, tool, or technique referenced in security reporting involving unintended information exposure through search or preview behavior.
Secret Service organization
The Secret Service is a U.S. federal law-enforcement agency that investigates certain financial and cybercrimes in addition to protecting leaders.
Secure email gateway product
A secure email gateway is a filter that checks incoming and outgoing email for spam, phishing, malware, and policy violations.
also: SEG
security control validation technique
The practice of testing whether security safeguards actually stop or detect realistic attacks.
security credentials concept
Security credentials are proof used to log in or gain access, such as passwords, keys, tokens, or certificates.
Security findings concept
Security findings are issues discovered during testing or review that may indicate weaknesses attackers could exploit.
Security fixes concept
Security fixes are software updates that repair weaknesses attackers could exploit.
Security flaws concept
Weaknesses or mistakes in software or systems that attackers may be able to exploit.
Security incident concept
A security incident is an event where systems, data, or accounts may have been attacked, exposed, or misused.
security information and event management tool
Security information and event management is a system that collects security logs and alerts from many sources so analysts can spot and investigate threats.
also: SIEM
security leaders concept
Security leaders are people responsible for guiding an organization’s cybersecurity strategy and teams.
security measures concept
Security measures are steps or tools used to reduce the chance or impact of security problems.
security posture concept
Security posture is the overall strength of an organization's defenses, risks, and readiness to handle cyber threats.
security professionals concept
Security professionals are people whose job is to protect systems, data, and organizations from security threats.
Security reports concept
Security reports are documents or alerts that explain threats, vulnerabilities, incidents, or defensive findings.
security risks concept
Security risks are possible ways that systems, data, or people could be harmed by accidents, weaknesses, or attacks.
security software product
Security software is software designed to protect computers, networks, or data from threats.
Security Standards concept
Documented requirements and best practices for protecting systems, data, and services.
security teams concept
Groups of professionals responsible for protecting an organization's information, systems, and networks from cyber threats.
security testing concept
Security testing is checking software, systems, or networks to find weaknesses before attackers can exploit them.
security tools tool
Security tools are software or hardware products used to detect, prevent, investigate, or respond to cyber threats.
security updates concept
Security updates are software fixes that close vulnerabilities or improve protection against threats.
Seed-Phrase Vishing technique
A phone-based scam in which criminals try to trick cryptocurrency users into revealing their wallet recovery words.
self-hosted concept
Self-hosted means an organization runs software on servers it controls instead of using a vendor's cloud service.
Self-Hosted Data Center Products product
Self-hosted Data Center products are software deployments that an organization runs on its own servers instead of using the vendor's cloud service.
Semiconductor concept
A semiconductor is a material used to make computer chips and other electronic components.
Semiconductor Industry concept
The semiconductor industry designs and makes electronic chips used in computers, phones, and many other devices.
sender concept
A sender is the person, account, server, or system that sends a message such as an email.
sensitive data concept
Sensitive data is information that could cause harm if exposed, such as passwords, financial details, or medical records.
sensitive files concept
Sensitive files are files that contain private, secret, or valuable information that should not be exposed to unauthorized people.
sensitive information concept
Sensitive information is data that should be protected because exposing it could harm a person, company, or system.
Sensitive personal information concept
Sensitive personal information is private data, such as identity, health, financial, or contact details, that could harm someone if exposed.
Sensitive records concept
Sensitive records are stored pieces of information that could harm people or organizations if exposed.
server-side-request-forgery vulnerability
Server-side request forgery is a vulnerability that lets an attacker make a server send requests to places the attacker should not be able to reach directly.
service account tokens concept
Service account tokens are digital credentials that let software or automated accounts access systems without a human logging in.
service accounts concept
Service accounts are accounts used by software or systems rather than by individual people.
service-account credentials concept
Service-account credentials are usernames, passwords, keys, or tokens used by automated software accounts.
Session forgery technique
An attack in which someone creates or changes login-session data so a system treats them as another user.
severity concept
Severity is a rating that describes how serious a security issue is.
SFV:NSPM concept
A Microsoft email-filtering classification indicating that a message was not marked as spam.
SHA-256 hashes concept
SHA-256 hashes are fixed-length digital fingerprints used to verify that data or files have not changed.
SHA-256 Password Storage technique
SHA-256 password storage means saving password-derived hashes using the SHA-256 algorithm, which can be unsafe when used without stronger password protections.
Shadowserver organization
Shadowserver is an internet security watchdog group that tracks exposed systems and other security data.
Shai-Hulud malware
Shai-Hulud is malware that has been described as targeting software supply chains and developer environments.
also: Shai-Hulud family
Shanghai Firetech Information Science and Technology organization
Shanghai Firetech Information Science and Technology is a company referenced in security reporting.
Shanghai State Security Bureau organization
The Shanghai State Security Bureau is a Chinese state-security organization referenced in security reporting.
Shared Findings Model concept
A shared findings model is a method for keeping security issues in one evidence-backed list so teams can track and fix them consistently.
shared infrastructure concept
Shared infrastructure is computing or network equipment used by multiple services, customers, or attackers.
Shared Service Account concept
A shared service account is a non-personal account used by multiple systems or people, which can make activity harder to trace.
Shared Web-Resource Library product
A shared web-resource library is reusable code used by multiple web applications to handle web files or resources.
Signing keys concept
Signing keys are cryptographic keys used to prove that software or data really came from a trusted publisher and was not changed.
SLA concept
An SLA, or service-level agreement, is a promise about how quickly or reliably a service will be delivered.
SLA tracking concept
The recording of whether work, such as fixing security issues, is completed within the promised time limit.
SMA organization
SMA is a company that makes solar inverters and energy-management equipment.
SMA 100 Series product
SMA 100 Series is SonicWall’s secure mobile access appliance line for remote access.
SMA 100 Series Product Line product
The SMA 100 Series is a SonicWall product line of remote-access security appliances.
SMA1000 product
SMA1000 is SonicWall’s secure mobile access appliance product line for remote access.
SMA1000 models 6210, 7210, and 8200v product
SMA1000 models 6210, 7210, and 8200v are specific SonicWall secure mobile access appliance models.
SMA1000-6210 product
SMA1000-6210 is a specific SonicWall SMA1000 secure mobile access appliance model.
smart contract concept
A smart contract is code on a blockchain that automatically carries out rules or transactions.
also: hardcoded smart contract address, smart contract state variables
Smart contracts concept
Smart contracts are programs stored on a blockchain that automatically run when agreed conditions are met.
SMB protocol
A network protocol used for providing shared access to files, printers, and serial ports, and a common target for ransomware and lateral movement.
Snapchat product
Snapchat is a messaging and social media app used to share photos and videos.
Snort tool
Snort is an open-source network intrusion detection and prevention tool used to spot suspicious traffic.
Snort Rules tool
Detection rules used by the Snort network-security tool to identify suspicious network traffic.
SOC 2 concept
SOC 2 is a common audit framework used to show that a service provider follows controls for security, availability, confidentiality, and related areas.
SOC 2 concept
SOC 2 is an audit framework that checks how a service provider protects customer data and operates security controls.
SOC 2 Type 1 concept
A SOC 2 audit report that assesses whether an organization's controls are properly designed at a specific point in time.
SOC 2 Type 2 concept
A SOC 2 audit report that assesses whether an organization's controls worked effectively over a period of time.
social engineering technique
Social engineering is manipulation of people into doing something or sharing information they otherwise would not.
social media concept
Social media means online platforms where people share messages, photos, videos, and other content.
Social Security organization
Social Security is a U.S. government program whose identifying numbers are often sensitive personal data targeted by criminals.
Social Security numbers concept
Social Security numbers are U.S. government identification numbers often targeted by criminals because they can be used for fraud.
socket organization
Socket is a software supply-chain security company that scans open-source packages for risky behavior.
Socket Threat Research organization
The threat research team at Socket, focusing on supply chain security and detecting malicious open-source packages.
SOCRadar organization
SOCRadar is a cybersecurity company that provides threat intelligence and external attack surface monitoring services.
Software flaws vulnerability
Software flaws are mistakes or weaknesses in programs that can cause bugs or create security risks.
Software Supply Chain Compromises technique
Software supply chain compromises are attacks in which criminals tamper with software, updates, dependencies, or development systems to reach downstream users.
also: supply chain poisoning, supply chain attacks
Software Versions concept
Numbered releases of a software product that identify which update or build is installed.
software vulnerabilities vulnerability
Software vulnerabilities are weaknesses in programs that attackers may use to gain access, steal data, or disrupt systems.
SonicWall organization
SonicWall is a cybersecurity vendor known for firewalls, secure remote access, and network security products.
SonicWall firewalls product
SonicWall firewalls are network security devices that inspect and control traffic entering or leaving a network.
SonicWall SMA1000 product
SonicWall SMA1000 is a secure mobile access appliance platform used for remote access to corporate networks.
Sou5 threat-actor
Sou5 is a threat-actor name referenced in security reporting.
Southern District of New York organization
The Southern District of New York is a federal judicial district that covers parts of New York and often handles major legal cases.
Southwark Crown Court organization
A Crown Court in London that handles serious criminal cases.
spearphishing-attachment technique
Spearphishing with an attachment is a targeted phishing attack that sends a malicious or deceptive file to a specific person or organization.
also: T1566.001, spearphishing attachment
Specialized Access product
A restricted program tier that gives approved organizations access to certain safety-testing capabilities.
SPF protocol
SPF is an email check that verifies whether a sending server is allowed to send email for a domain.
also: spf=pass
Spotify product
Spotify is a digital music, podcast, and audio streaming service.
SpringBoard product
The core iOS process that manages the home screen, app launching, and much of the user interface.
springboard-injection technique
A named malware technique or artifact referenced in security reporting.
SQL injection technique
SQL injection is a web attack where malicious database commands are inserted into an application's input fields or requests.
SSL VPN protocol
SSL VPN is a type of remote access connection that uses SSL-based security to connect users to a private network.
SSL VPN gateways product
SSL VPN gateways are remote-access systems that let users connect securely to private networks through encrypted web-based VPN connections.
ssrf vulnerability
A type of web vulnerability where an attacker tricks a server into making unintended requests to internal systems or external sites.
staging technique
Staging is the act of preparing data, tools, or files in an intermediate location before they are used, moved, or stolen.
Stale concept
Stale means something is old or not recently used and may need review, updating, or removal.
State Threats concept
Cybersecurity threats posed by governments or groups acting on their behalf.
Stolen concept
Stolen means taken without permission, such as stolen passwords, data, or devices.
stolen credentials concept
Stolen credentials are usernames, passwords, or login tokens that attackers have obtained without permission.
stolen data concept
Stolen data is information taken without permission, often later sold, leaked, or used for extortion.
stolen information concept
Stolen information is data taken without permission, such as personal details, business files, passwords, or financial records.
Stored cross-site scripting vulnerability
Stored cross-site scripting is a web vulnerability where malicious script is saved on a site and later runs in visitors' browsers.
Streaming Royalty Fraud technique
Streaming royalty fraud is faking music plays to collect payments intended for legitimate artists and rights holders.
Subdomain Label concept
A subdomain label is one part of a domain name that appears before the main domain, such as "mail" in mail.example.com.
also: subdomain, landing host
suicide concept
Suicide is the act of intentionally ending one's own life and is often treated as harmful content when discussed in online safety contexts.
supervised release concept
Supervised release is a court-ordered period after prison when a person must follow legal conditions while monitored.
Supplier organization
A supplier is a company or person that provides goods or services to another organization.
supply chain concept
A supply chain is the network of vendors, software, services, and processes an organization depends on to operate.
Supply Chain Compromises technique
Attacks that reach victims by tampering with a trusted supplier, software dependency, update, or distribution process.
Supply chain malware campaign technique
An attack campaign that spreads harmful code through trusted software packages or suppliers.
Supply-chain campaign technique
A supply-chain campaign is an attack that reaches victims by compromising a trusted supplier, service, or software component.
Supreme Court organization
The Supreme Court is the highest court in a legal system, such as the United States Supreme Court.
surveillance concept
The act of monitoring people or activities, often covertly, as part of espionage, law enforcement, or malware functions like keyloggers.
Suspicious messages concept
Suspicious messages are emails, texts, or chats that may be scams, phishing attempts, or signs of compromise.
Swift tool
Swift is a programming language created by Apple for building apps and software.
Tabletop exercise technique
A tabletop exercise is a practice discussion where teams walk through a simulated emergency or cyberattack to test their plans.
tabletop exercises technique
Tabletop exercises are practice sessions where teams walk through a simulated crisis to test plans and decision-making.
Take Control product
Take Control is a remote access and support product used by IT teams to connect to customer devices.
TAKEOVER technique
TAKEOVER is a named account-control or exploitation step referenced in security reporting.
Talos organization
Talos, also known as Cisco Talos, is Cisco's threat intelligence and security research organization.
target lists concept
Target lists are collections of people, systems, organizations, or addresses selected for scanning, monitoring, or attack.
Target Selection technique
Target selection is the process attackers use to choose which people, organizations, or systems to attack.
tcpip.sys product
tcpip.sys is a Windows system driver that handles core TCP/IP network communications.
Technical analysis concept
Technical analysis is a detailed examination of how a system, vulnerability, malware sample, or attack works.
Technical findings concept
Technical findings are the concrete details a researcher discovers, such as what was vulnerable, exposed, or misconfigured.
telegram
Telegram is a messaging app that supports channels, groups, bots, and encrypted chats.
Telemetry concept
Telemetry is data automatically collected from systems or devices to show what they are doing and whether something looks wrong.
tenant concept
A tenant is a separate customer space inside a shared cloud or software service.
text messages concept
Short Message Service (SMS) messages, commonly used for two-factor authentication codes but susceptible to interception.
The Block organization
The Block is a news and research organization focused on cryptocurrency and digital assets.
The Information organization
The Information is a technology-focused news publication that reports on companies, startups, and the tech industry.
The Putin Tax organization
The Putin Tax is a report examining the economic costs of hostile activity linked to Russia.
Third-Party Compromise technique
Third-party compromise is a breach of a supplier, partner, or service provider that creates risk for another organization.
third-party service concept
A third-party service is an outside provider’s system or software that an organization depends on.
third-party vendors organization
Third-party vendors are outside companies that provide products or services to an organization.
Third-Party Vulnerability Disclosure Policy concept
A third-party vulnerability disclosure policy explains how an organization reports security flaws it finds in another company’s products.
Threat actors concept
Threat actors are people or groups that carry out harmful activity against computers, websites, or organizations.
threat intelligence concept
Threat intelligence is information collected and analyzed about possible or active cyber threats.
also: Cloudforce One threat intelligence
threats concept
Threats are possible dangers that could harm systems, data, devices, or users.
Time-Locked Vaults concept
Storage systems that prevent funds or data from being accessed or moved until a set waiting period has passed.
also: time-locked storage
Timestamps concept
Timestamps are recorded dates and times that show when something happened, such as when a file was created or changed.
tldriver tool
A malicious npm package referenced in security reporting.
tlxbnhd tool
A malicious npm package referenced in security reporting.
token concept
A digital piece of data used for authentication, authorization, or as a session identifier.
tokens concept
Digital objects used for authentication, identification, or authorization, like access tokens.
Tomcat product
Tomcat is a widely used open-source Java web server and servlet container for running Java web applications.
Tomcat Application Context concept
A Tomcat application context is the defined web application area and URL space in an Apache Tomcat server.
Tomcat RewriteValve tool
An Apache Tomcat configuration feature that can rewrite, redirect, or block web requests using rules.
Tomcat RewriteValve Rules technique
Tomcat RewriteValve rules are Apache Tomcat settings that rewrite or block web requests before they reach an application.
tooling concept
Tooling means the software and utilities people use to perform tasks such as development, testing, or security operations.
Tor2Mine threat-actor
Tor2Mine is a threat group associated with installing cryptocurrency-mining malware on compromised systems.
ToUnicode Maps protocol
ToUnicode maps are PDF tables that map encoded character values to readable Unicode text.
also: ToUnicode
tracking concept
Monitoring of online behavior, often through cookies and scripts, for advertising or malicious profiling.
Traffic baseline concept
A record of normal network activity used to spot unusual behavior.
